controls.title: Synthetic authenticated-encryption round trip
Wrong synthetic credential fails closed
KDF parameters remain within approved bounds
Unknown, oversized, nested, bulk, and wallet-shaped input is rejected
Corrupted synthetic envelopes fail closed
Reports expose no fixture credential or wallet-shaped material
Production source contains no VaultLab import, fixture, or credential marker
Security agents return recommendations without execution authority
Security events reject commands, transactions, targets, and credential material
Evidence envelopes bind a passing report to an exact source revision
Signing-intent policy accepts sanitized classifications and rejects transaction or secret material
Signing-intent decisions require a human and never grant signing or execution authority
Recovery requires independent legal, security, and custody approval
Recovery transitions preserve authority, approvals, waiting policy, notifications, and finding gates
Native-custody readiness requires all twelve controls and zero critical or high findings
Native-custody assessment is staging-only and cannot activate deployment, signing, or asset movement
Withdrawal policy rejects raw values and blocks takeover, compliance, limit, authentication, cooldown, and approval failures
Withdrawal decisions require separate human authorization and cannot hold, sign, or move assets
Release provenance requires all fourteen build controls and zero open security findings
Release assessment accepts digests only and cannot deploy, sign, activate custody, or move assets
Incident lifecycle preserves severity, completed controls, approvals, phase order, and closure quorum
Incident decisions cannot contain, revoke, deploy, sign, or move assets
Privileged-access policy rejects raw identity, credential, token, command, and target material
Privileged-access decisions enforce JIT, MFA, reauthentication, session, SoD, change-window, and approval evidence without granting access
Ledger-integrity readiness requires all fourteen segregation, accounting, reconciliation, reserve-method, monitoring, and replay controls
Ledger evidence contains digests and classifications only and cannot establish solvency, mutate balances, trade, withdraw, sign, or move assets
Break-glass governance preserves phase order, authority evidence, quorum, immutable time limits, revocation, sealed evidence, and independent closure
Break-glass records cannot grant access, start sessions, execute revocation, deploy, sign, or move assets
API and session policy rejects raw secrets, tokens, credentials, keys, payloads, identities, addresses, signatures, and transactions
API and session decisions enforce registration, least privilege, mTLS, request signing, replay, rate, idempotency, revocation, lifetime, and approval evidence without executing requests
Signer-ceremony governance preserves architecture, forward-only phases, three-role quorum, monotonic controls, append-only approvals, sealed evidence, and independent review
Signer-ceremony inputs reject shares, keys, seeds, entropy values, transcript content, credentials, signatures, and commands and cannot activate a signer
Resilience readiness requires all fourteen backup, isolation, integrity, restore, replay, reconciliation, failover, monitoring, and independent-review controls
Resilience evidence contains digests and classifications only and cannot restore, fail over, mutate data, deploy, sign, or move assets
Secret-leakage readiness requires all twelve log, trace, crash, artifact, support, telemetry, entropy, redaction, canary, ruleset, and review controls
Secret-leakage evidence contains counts and digests only and cannot revoke credentials, delete artifacts, grant access, deploy, sign, or move assets
Immutable-audit readiness requires all fourteen append-only, chain, sequence, time, identity, access, retention, replication, export, schema, alert, and review controls
Audit-integrity evidence contains digests and counts only and cannot read, write, delete, repair, mutate, deploy, sign, or move assets
Security exceptions enforce forward-only phases, independent quorum, monotonic controls, immutable expiry, a thirty-day ceiling, and no critical-risk waiver
Security-exception records reject operational and secret material and cannot grant exceptions, bypass policy, remediate, deploy, sign, or move assets
Client-integrity readiness requires all fourteen distribution, signature, reproducibility, binary, attestation, hardware, anti-tamper, update, rollback, redaction, and review controls
Client evidence rejects attestation tokens, device identifiers, binaries, credentials, keys, and wallet data and cannot activate, distribute, update, access a device, store keys, sign, or move assets
Market-data readiness requires all fourteen source, authenticity, freshness, sequence, outlier, quorum, circuit-breaker, failover, replay, isolation, and review controls
Market-data evidence rejects feeds, prices, symbols, credentials, orders, trades, and transactions and cannot publish prices, trade, execute orders, mutate limits, or make financial claims

Availability readiness requires all fourteen isolation, synthetic-traffic, blast-radius, rate, backpressure, queue, breaker, shedding, degraded-mode, timeout, failover, recovery, observability, and review controls

Availability evidence is isolated-test or staging only, rejects commands, targets, hosts, URLs, traffic, and credentials, and cannot generate traffic, execute chaos, fail over, remediate, deploy, sign, or move assets
Vulnerability remediation requires all fourteen inventory, intake, severity, ownership, SLA, exposure, provenance, retest, regression, closure, and exception-governance controls
Vulnerability evidence rejects exploit details, targets, credentials, raw findings, and wallet material and cannot scan, exploit, remediate, patch, deploy, sign, or move assets
External-assessment readiness requires all fourteen authorization, scope, rules, safe-harbor, independence, safety, handling, severity, retention, and closure-review controls
External-assessment evidence rejects attacks, exploits, targets, credentials, payloads, and wallet material and cannot scan, exploit, generate traffic, access devices, grant access, or remediate
Privacy minimization requires all fourteen inventory, purpose, collection, allowlist, classification, encryption, least-privilege, retention, deletion, backup, redaction, rights, and review controls

Privacy evidence rejects personal data, identifiers, credentials, raw records, and wallet material and cannot access raw data, delete data, mutate retention, grant access, remediate, deploy, sign, or move assets
